TcAttribute.description: This property defines the length of individual segments used to make up the entire fill area.The Segment Length should have a positive value to specify the length of the fill area.
This property indicates the fillet type to be used for the weld. Valid values are: Fillet T-Joint, Fillet Lap Joint, and Fillet Corner Joint; null value is allowed if the fillet type is unspecified.
This property indicates the contour type to be used for the weld. Valid values are: Convex, Concave, Flush, and None; null value is allowed if the contour type is unspecified.
This property indicates the method for accomplishing the weld. Valid values are: Continuous and Skip; null value is allowed if the method is unspecified.
This property indicates the joint configuration, which can be: butt, corner, T-joint or Lap. Null value is allowed if the joint configuration is unspecified.
This property indicates the type of groove weld, which can be: square, bevel, J, V, U, flared bevel or flared V. Null value is allowed if the groove type is unspecified.
This property indicates that the specific weld should contain a bead of fillet weld. Null value is allowed if this is not the case.
This property specifies the type of Groove Weld; null value is allowed when type is unspecified.
This property indicates the contour type to be used for the weld. Valid values are: Convex, Concave, Flush, and None; null value is allowed when contour type is unspecified.
This property indicates the method for accomplishing the weld. Valid values are: Continuous and Skip; null value is allowed when method is unspecified.
This property is used to indicate that the specific weld should contain a bead of fillet weld; null value is allowed when type is unspecified.
This property Used to indicate the joint configuration, which can be: butt, corner, T-joint or Lap. Null value is allowed when joint configuration is unspecified.

This property defines the cross section shape of the 'top' of the weld, which can have the following values: contour, concave, flat or none. Null value is allowed when cross section shape is unspecified.
This indicates the weld process (e.g. Metal Inert Gas or MIG, Tungsten Inert Gas) used for creating the Cpd0ArcWeld object.

TcClass.description: This object serves as container for all content authored in CPD

TcAttribute.description: This property models the volume of Cpd0ContinuousJoin object.
This property models the length of Cpd0ContinuousJoin object.
This Boolean property specifies if Cpd0Datum controls x-direction in coordinate space.
This Boolean property specifies if Cpd0Datum controls y- direction in coordinate space.
This Boolean property specifies if Cpd0Datum controls z-direction in coordinate space.
This property references a CAD description of Cpd0Datum, i.e. the associated Cpd0ShapeDesignRevision object. Its value can be null if there is no such object reference.

This property specifies the direction that the Cpd0atum will lock the component in. It is measured against absolute coordinate system in the CAD system, and represented by configurable values. Null value is allowed.
This property specifies the name of the plane in coordinate system used to generate the Cpd0atum. Null value is allowed.
This property defines the X value for a normal vector that defines the plane used in the Cpd0atum definition. Null value is allowed.
This property defines the Y value for a normal vector that defines the plane used in the Cpd0atum definition. Null value is allowed.
This property defines the Z value for a normal vector that defines the plane used in the Cpd0atum definition. Null value is allowed.
This property defines the X value for a normal vector that defines the axis used in the Cpd0atum definition. Null value is allowed.
This property defines the Y value for a normal vector that defines the axis used in the Cpd0atum definition. Null value is allowed.
This property indicates that this specific Cpd0atum is derived from another Cpd0atum. Null value is allowed.
This property defines the Z value for a normal vector that defines the axis used in the Cpd0atum definition. Null value is allowed.
This property stores a tagged reference to the Shape Design Item Revision for Reuse and Subordinate category Cpd0DesignElements. It cannot be NULL.
This property is used to store the identifier of the Cpd0DesignControlElement object.It cannot be NULL.

TcClass.description: Represents Occurrences of Design Items within a CPD

TcAttribute.description: Identifier of this Cpd0DesignFeature object. This required property cannot be null.

The design model element in the target model (Cpd0CollaborativeDesign) that represents the Item that was instantiated.NULL is not allowed, since the Cpd0DesignItemInstance processing to create or update a realization requires a valid reuse object.
This is the latest last modified date of any level of structure in the source Item assembly.
This Boolean property is true, if the source Item of associated Reuse Cpd0DesignElement (see attribute cpd0reuse_element) is an Installation Assembly.

TcClass.description: Represents Occurrences of various kinds of Designs

TcAttribute.description: This property is a reference to a parent Cpd0DesignModelElement object for presentation purposes, it can be null when no parent exists.
This is an identifier that is intended to be unique within the presented parent.
This property specifies the type name of a concrete DesignModelElementState. The List of Values Cpd0Categories contains the allowed values for this property.
This specifies the identifier of the Cpd0DesignModelElement object, it cannot be null.

This property is applicable for Reuse and Subordinate category objects. It is set by the realization update process, and indicates if the referenced source object was an assembly when the realization was last updated.

This property is used by, also its value is explicitly set by, NX application. On Subordinate category objects, its value is copied from "UG ENTITY HANDLE" occurrence note property on realized item occurrences.
This property specifies unique identifier of occurrence thread in parent's source object for realized item structure, its value is empty if object is not a Subordinate category object.
This specifies the ItemRevision object that is occurring.
Defines the group that the weld is a member of, as established in NX. It may be null.
Defines the number of panels being joined by the weld. It may be null.
Specifies the total number of welds in a specific group. It may be null.
Indicates whether the weld has passed all of the Weld Advisor checks the last time they were executed. Yes indicated all checks passed. It may be null.
Distinguishes between welds that are 'fixed' and those that are 'associative' in NX. It may be null.

cpd0FindNum helps identify an object in Design Subset Element of a Workset. Useful primarily in sharing of PLM BOM data with ERP system.The purpose is the same as the Find Number used in the Structure Manager application.
Represents the quantity of the stock which is required by the Design Component. This is primarily used and set by CAD applications.
Represents the Unit of Measure of the Stock Quantity property
The resistance value to be used for the spot weld. It may be null.
This attribute describes the key metal panel in the stackup that is used to determine specific weld parameters. It may be null.Example: 1.20GG
This attribute defines the metal combination of the spot weld depicted as... G1.2G-G1.5G. The G represents the surface coating and the number is the metal gauge.It may be null.
Indicates this is a Dimensional Control spot weld.It may be null.
Indicates this is a Key Product Characteristics weld.It may be null.
Specifies the justification used to indicate that the weld is of type, KPC.It may be null.
Indicates this is a Process Control spot weld.It may be null.
This attribute defines the part stack up order using the same value as defined by the Part Number attribute in the Weld preferences.It may be null.Example: 25865934-25865936
This specifies the minimum number of points per group that are required to be welded.It may be null.
This indicates the required surface finish of the weld. It may be null.
Refers to the symbol name used to depict the specific weld. Used primarily for RobScan welds.It may be null.
This attribute defines the weld force to be used for this spot weld.It may be null.

TcAttribute.description: This references the containing application model for the shape. Since a delegate object and Cpd0ShapeDesign exist in the context of an application model, this property cannot be null.
This specifies the unique identifier of the delegate object. This is a string property computed based on delegate object unique identifier.

Thickness of surface add. It may be null.
Indicates the weld process (MIG, TIG, etc) used for the weld.It may be null.
Surface type (Smooth, Glue etc).It may be null.

This property is added if the Collaborative Product Development template is also installed, it references an associated reuse object if applicable (e.g. if the element is a subordinate, the reference will be to its reuse), it is null otherwise.
This property references the overriding Cpd0ShapeDesignRevision object if it exists, can be null otherwise.
This property specifies any NX Alternate Representation for this object, it can be null if none exists.

This operation also allows to attach an extension as post action where users can write their own ITK implementation to map attributes.

Dataset to represent 4G Easy Preview Information.

TcStandardType.description: This is an instantiable sub-type of the abstract business object Cpd0ContinuousJoin and refers to a bead of material that traverses across a face of a part or parts.Cpd0AdhesiveBead is primarily used by CAD applications such as NX. The cross section of the shape is defined in the CAD space as well as the specific path of the bead. The material of the bead may be structural adhesive or arc weld material. The length and volume of the bead is included in the CAD definition.This is a generic business object, and can be further sub-typed to meet any special requirements a site may have.

This is an instantiable sub-type of abstract business object Cpd0DiscreteJoin that models adhesive dollops, and refers to a drop of material that is typically some sort of structural adhesive.This is primarily used by CAD applications such as NX. It is defined in CAD by a specific coordinate location and the dollop material type.This is a generic business object, and can be further sub-typed to meet any special requirements a site may have.

This business object models a type of Cpd0SurfaceAdd called Adhesive Fill, and refers to an area where sealer/adhesive material is built up in a given boundary.This is primarily used by CAD application such as NX, which also defines the boundary and amount of measured build up. The material used for the build-up is usually some sort of structural adhesive.This is a generic business object, and can be further sub-typed to meet any special requirements a site may have.

This business object models a type of Cpd0ArcWeld wherein material is added to join parts together typically perpendicular to each other or at an angle to each other.The cross section of this weld will look like a right triangle; its size is usually conveyed by defining either the legs of this triangle or its throat thickness.This business object is primarily used by CAD application such as NX; and this generic business object can be further sub-typed to meet any special requirements a site may have.

Cpd0ArcGrooveWeld models a type of Cpd0ArcWeld wherein material is added to join butted plates together.This weld is characterized by a cross section of one of the following: butt, bevel, V, J, U, flared bevel or flared V; and typically joins parts end to end.This business object is primarily used by CAD application such as NX; and it can be further sub-typed to meet any special requirements a site may have.

Cpd0ArcPlugSlotWeld models a type of Cpd0ArcWeld, where material is added to join overlapping plates together.The Cpd0PlugSlotWeld is defined by filling in a hole or slot in one part that sits atop another part, and it is primarily used by CAD applications such as NX.This is a generic business object that can be extended by Teamcenter deployments if necessary.

Cpd0ArcSpotWeld models a type of Cpd0DiscreteJoin which is created using one or more locating points where spot welds are made between two overlapping parts. Arc welding is used to create a small "spot" that is quickly heated to the melting point.The Cpd0ArcSpotWeld effectively joins parts together at the spot. It is primarily used by CAD applications such as NX and is defined in the CAD model by indicating the coordinates of the spot locations.This is a generic business object that can be extended by Teamcenter deployments if necessary.

This abstract class falls under Cpd0ContinuousJoin sub-type of Cpd0DesignFeature objects; and represents some forms of continuous arc welds.This business object is used by NX, and users need to choose Cpd0DesignElement objects in the same Cpd0CollaborativeDesign to create these.This is a generic business object that can be sub-typed to create specific types of continuous arc welds.

Cpd0AssociatedDatasetRel is relation to attach Dataset (Associated Dataset) to Cpd0DesignFeature. Cpd0AssociatedDatasetRel is subclass of Mdl0CopyStableRelation and Design Feature is primary in the relation.Associated Data is NX data file containing information NX needs to track and manage the weld feature is the secondary in the relation.Cpd0AssociatedDatasetRel is inheritable and revisable. This is used by 4GD and NX.

Cpd0AttachInfoInContext is a relationship used for capturing context specific information. The information is captured in a Cpd0InfoInContext Attribute Group. The Attribute Group is related to an object (one that provides the context) using this relation.Cpd0AttachInfoInContext captures Find Numbers for Design Components. Find Numbers are associated with Design Components in the context of a given Workset. Cpd0AttachInfoInContext associates the Cpd0InfoInContext Attribute Group to the realization map object of the Design Subset Element in the Workset.This way the Find Number is assigned to the Design Component in the context of the Workset.

Cpd0CollDesignToToplineBVR represents relation between Product Design and Top Line BOM View Revision when realization is done through 4g_easy application.
Cpd0CollDesignToToplineBVR relation provides ability to traverse from DesignElement to its corresponding Bomline in context of a Top Line.

Cpd0CollaborativeDesign is a container for a product that is developed by design team(s) in course of a collaborative development activity.Cpd0CollaborativeDesign is populated by model elements such as Design Components, Design Features and these elements can be organized via Partitions. Contributors (with appropriate access) can add new elements to Cpd0CollaborativeDesign from Teamcenter or a CAD system, or they can realize existing items/item assemblies into a Product Design. Cpd0CollaborativeDesign can be configured (e.g. by means of Effectivity or Revision Rules ). Its content can be searched (with Partitions, Attributes or Spatial Criteria).Cpd0CollaborativeDesign is a generic business object widely used by 4th Generation Design (typically among the initial objects created for a product) and associated applications.

TcProperty.description: This property denotes Saved Variant Rules created in 4th Generation Design application in context of the Cpd0CollaborativeDesign object.

TcStandardType.description: Design Features are related to the Design Components they connect via a relation Cpd0ConnectedElement.Cpd0DesignFeature is primary and Cpd0DesignElement is secondary in the relation.Cpd0ConnectedElement relationships have a copy-stable ID which is unique within the scope of the Design Feature. The copy stable ID can be specified on create; if not specified, they will be automatically generated by Teamcenter. The copy stable ID is used by external applications, like CAD, to correlate internal data to the related objectsCpd0ConnectedElement relation object is used by 4GD application consumers such as CAD tools and is minor versionable and inheritable.

This abstract class represents any form of continuous join of materials, such as an arc weld or glue, where the connected elements are Cpd0DesignElement objects from the same Cpd0CollaborativeDesign.This is a generic business object; sites can use the available subtypes or extend this further to create specific subtypes of joins depending on requirements.

Cpd0ControlModel business object is a relation which links Cpd0DesignControlElement (Design Control Elements) and Cpd0DesignElement (Design Components) or Cpd0DesignFeature (Design Features). Design Control Elements are primary in the relation and Design Feature/Design Component been secondary.Cpd0ControlModel relation is created when a weld is created between design components.Cpd0ControlModel relation object is used by 4th Generation Design application. Cpd0ControlModel is minor versionable and inheritable.

This is an abstract business object that represents some forms of datum.Datum features are authored in CAD system such as NX and consumed by Manufacturing Process Management (e.g. to position tools or as measurement points), but these are managed in Teamcenter as Cpd0DesignFeature objects.Each datum point is associated with a position and corresponding x, y, z coordinates in product space.Teamcenter provides two types of instantiable Cpd0Datum objects: Cpd0PinDatum and Cpd0SurfaceDatum.

TcProperty.description: This is a runtime array property that represents position of the Cpd0Datum as an array of double values.

TcStandardType.description: This provides a common functionality to manage physical design content, such as Cpd0DesignElement and Cpd0DesignFeature objects, in a product through a control model that represents a more abstract concept of the design ( for example, a weld seam or a mechanical routing path ). As a product evolves, new revisions of Cpd0DesignControlElement may share common objects as some Cpd0DesignFeatures or Cpd0DesignElements may change, while referencing new revisions of the changed objects. A Cpd0ControlModel relation owned by Cpd0DesignControlElement relates the Cpd0DesignElement and Cpd0DesignFeature objects that it manages.Cpd0DesignControlElements are used by CAD tools via 4th Generation Design application service operations.

This represents use of a design, a component or a design assembly in the context of a product.Cpd0DesignElement objects are the basic building blocks that populate a Cpd0CollaborativeDesign; as users create, edit, configure and perform actions on these objects such as revise, save-as or apply status via a Workflow. Depending on their setting, Cpd0DesignElements can be categorized as Shape, Reuse, Subordinate or Promissory which is indicative of their current role in the product.This is a generic business object widely used by 4GD ( typically a large number of Cpd0DesignElement objects can be found under Cpd0CollaborativeDesign object for a product ) and associated applications such as NX; and can be further extended depending on any special requirements of a deployment.

TcProperty.description: This runtime property references a thumbnail dataset for this Cpd0DesignElement. A null value is allowed and indicates no thumbnail dataset is associated.
This references a list of Ptn0Partition objects where this Cpd0DesignElement object has a Ptn0Membership.

Boolean property that if true indicates the referenced source Item Revision is not the latest having status. This is relevant only to Reuse category Cpd0DesignElement objects, it is set to null for other categories.
Boolean property that returns true if Source structure is updated after Reuse Cpd0DesignElement object was last updated.
Boolean property that returns true if the source Item Revision is frozen (and BVR, if it exists for configured view, is precise).
This runtime property represents all the subordinate Cpd0DesignElement objects if this Cpd0DesignElement is Reuse category. Value is null if category is other than Reuse.
This points to attached objects via the Cpd0GeometricCut relation to this Cpd0DesignElement.A null value is allowed, and indicates there are no attached objects with this relation.

TcStandardType.description: This abstract class models elements or characteristics of a product design such as welds, seams, connections and routings.A Cpd0DesignFeature may be associated with several revisions of a Cpd0DesignControlElement that manages these objects along with connected Cpd0DesignElements.

TcProperty.description: This relation, owned by Cpd0DesignFeature, specifies which Cpd0DesignElements are connected to this object.
This relation gives attached Datasets created by a CAD system that represent geometry of this Cpd0DesignFeature.

TcStandardType.description: This manages the item realization of item assembly content into a product design. Cpd0DesignItemInstance objects are created when user initiates item realization operation using an existing item assembly content in Teamcenter or NX. The outcome of item realization is one or more Reuse and Subordinate category Cpd0DesignElement objects. These objects get updated when user updates item realization interactively or via a Workflow Handler.Cpd0DesignItemInstance is a generic object that can be further extended for specific deployment as needed; it is widely used by 4th Generation Design (typically to migrate existing item assembly data into a product design), NX and associated applications.

This Business Object models an abstract class to represent all components positioned in the context of a product (e.g. Cpd0DesignElement objects in a Cpd0CollaborativeDesign). This is the parent class for the concrete Cpd0DesignElement business object which is the primary building block of a product or product design activity in a 4th Generation Design application.This abstract business object is generic and can be further sub-typed by a deployment if the out-of-the-box sub-type Cpd0DesignElement needs to be extended to suit their requirements.The instantiable sub-types of this ( example: Cpd0DesignElement ) are widely used in 4th Generation Design and NX applications

TcProperty.description: This references Cpd0DesignFeature objects that reference this object as a connected element via the Cpd0ConnectedElement relation.

TcStandardType.description: Cpd0DiscreteJoin business object represents a weld join.This business object is not authored and updated in the NX application as it is an abstract Business Object. This business object cannot be authored or updated through Teamcenter. It is a type of Design Feature. Its subtypes are attached to the Cpd0DesignElement with the Cpd0ConnectedElement relation. Discrete joins include rivets, nuts, studs, and other mechanical joins. You can create subtypes of discrete joins, for example, weld join may be an arc spot weld or resistance weld. To add or change the available joins or their subtypes, you can customize the relevant objects in the Business Modeler IDE.Subtypes of this object are used by the NX and 4GD applications.

TcProperty.description: Runtime property of a position of the discrete join. It is not supported at the Cpd0DiscreteJoin type, but subtypes may give a value here. For example, a Cpd0Datum has a co-ordinate point for its position.It may be null.

TcStandardType.description: Cpd0GeometricCut relation is created between the cutting tool and the design component cut by the tool. Both primary and secondary in the relation are of type Cpd0DesignModelElement.A geometric cut is a CAD-authored geometric relationship in a product design between a CAD-authored positioned model element and a positioned cutting tool. Shape overrides on a shape design component might be due to geometric cuts in the shape using cutting tools. CAD tools track which cutting tools are the cause of the shape override. The cutting tools are related to the shape designs being cut by it.Cpd0GeometricCut relation object is used by 4GD applications and is inheritable.

Cpd0InfoInContext is an Attribute Group to store information that is specific to a given context. Out of the box this is used for capturing Find Numbers for Design Components.Find Number for a Design Component is specific to the context provided by a Workset and Design Subset Element. So, Cpd0InfoInContext is associated to a corresponding realization map (Rlz0ModelRealizationMap) using the Cpd0AttachInfoInContext relation.

A relationship for tracking the original object stock part that this was created from. It has additional properties to describe the physical details of the stock being used. For example: the length of the stock.
A relationship for tracking the original object that this was created from.

Cpd0MechanicalClinch business object represents a mechanical join in NX application. This business object is authored and updated in the NX application. This business object cannot be authored or updated through Teamcenter. It is a type of Discrete Join. It is attached to the Cpd0DesignElement with the Cpd0ConnectedElement relation. Cpd0MechanicalClinch is the primary object in Cpd0ConnectedElement relation with Design Component. MechanicalClinch joins thin metal sheet without additional components, it is a special tool to plastically form an interlock between two or more sheets. This object is used by the NX and 4GD applications.

Cpd0PinDatum business object represents a datum in the NX application. This business object is authored and updated through NX. This object cannot be authored or updated through Teamcenter. It is a type of Datum. It is attached to the Cpd0DesignElement with the Cpd0ConnectedElement relation. Cpd0PinDatum is the primary object in Cpd0ConnectedElement relation with Design Component. It is a reference point on an object against which measurements are made.This object is used by the NX and 4GD applications.

Cpd0ResistanceWeld business object represents a weld in NX. This object is authored and updated through NX. This object cannot be authored in Teamcenter. This object cannot be updated through Teamcenter. It is a type of Discrete Join. It has Cpd0ConnectedElement relation with Design Component. Cpd0ResistanceWeld is the primary object in Cpd0ConnectedElement relation with Design Component.This object is used by the NX and 4GD applications.

Cpd0Rivet business object represents a weld in NX application. This business object is authored and updated in the NX application. This business object cannot be authored or updated through Teamcenter. It is a type of Discrete Join. It is attached to the Cpd0DesignElement with the Cpd0ConnectedElement relation. Cpd0Rivet is the primary object in Cpd0ConnectedElement relation with Design Component. It is a metal pin for passing through holes in two or more plates or pieces to hold them together usually made with a head at one end the other end being hammered into head after insertion.This object is used by the NX and 4GD applications.

This models the source object Item for delegate shape objects such as 'shape' category Cpd0DesignElement, Cpd0DesignControlElement and Cpd0Datum objects.Cpd0ShapeDesign is the parent Item for the Cpd0ShapeDesignRevisions that reference the CAD data, and in turn are referenced by Shape category Cpd0DesignElement objects that represent the product-specific geometry in a product design. Teamcenter creates a Cpd0ShapeDesign object when user creates a delegate such as a category shape Cpd0DesignElement object; and operations that result in creation of new versions ( saveAs, revise ) of such delegate objects results in creation of new associated Cpd0ShapeDesign objects.Cpd0ShapeDesign is used by 4th Generation Design application, and can be further extended to meet any special requirements.

TcProperty.description: Object that the shape design delegates right to. The delegate object type is a Cpd0DesignElement, a Cpd0Datum or a Cpd0DesignControlElement.

TcStandardType.description: Form Storage object for "Cpd0ShapeDesignMaster" business object
Master Form Storage Class of ShapeDesignRevision
ItemRevision object for "Cpd0ShapeDesign" business object

Cpd0SubsetDefaults is a sub-type of Attribute Group (Mdl0AttributeGroup) used to store target properties for model content added into a subset in a workset (Cpd0DesignSubsetElement residing within a Cpd0WorksetRevision).Cpd0SubetDefaults may be related (via Mdl0AttachAttrGroup) to a single Cpd0DesignSubsetElement.Create or update of subset content via some service operations (e.g. supporting Cpd0::Soa::CpdCore::_2015_07::DataManagement::DesignSubsetsInfo and its list of elements in applyTargetPropertiesToElements) allows setting desired target effectivity, variants and partition memberships (see attributes on parent classes) on elements being added to a subset (Cpd0DesignSubsetElement) in a workset (Cpd0WorksetRevision).Cpd0SubetDefaults is used by core 4GD (4th Generation Design) applications, but it may also be extended by sub-classing if there are more application specific defaults to be stored (however, such applications will have to provide behavior to set such additional defaults.)

Cpd0SurfaceAdd business object represents a surface weld.This business object is not authored and updated in the NX application as it is an abstract Business Object. This business object cannot be authored or updated through Teamcenter. It is a type of Design Feature. Its subtypes are attached to the Cpd0DesignElement with the Cpd0ConnectedElement relation. SurfaceAdd includes AdhesiveFill and SurfaceWeld. You can create subtypes of surfaceadd. To add or change the available surfaceadd or their subtypes, you can customize the relevant objects in the Business Modeler IDE.Subtypes of this object are used by the NX and 4GD applications

Cpd0SurfaceDatum business object represents a datum in the NX application. This business object is authored and updated through NX. This object cannot be authored or updated through Teamcenter. It is a type of Datum. It is attached to the Cpd0DesignElement with the Cpd0ConnectedElement relation. Cpd0SurfaceDatum is the primary object in Cpd0ConnectedElement relation with Design Component. It is a surface on a work piece that establishes a datum. This object is used by the NX and 4GD applications.

Cpd0SurfaceWeld business object represents a weld in NX application. This business object is authored and updated in the NX application. This business object cannot be authored or updated through Teamcenter. It is a type of SurfaceAdd Weld. It is attached to the Cpd0DesignElement with the Cpd0ConnectedElement relation. Cpd0SurfaceWeld is the primary object in Cpd0ConnectedElement relation with Design Component. This type of weld is used to build up the new surfaces or replace the metal on worn-out surfaces.This object is used by the NX and 4GD applications.

Cpd0WeldNut business object represents a weld in the NX application. This business object is authored and updated through NX. This object cannot be authored or updated through Teamcenter. It is a type of discrete join. It is connected to the Cpd0DesignElements with the Cpd0ConnectedElement relation. Cpd0WeldNut is the primary object in Cpd0ConnectedElement relation with Design Component. It is a special type of nut specifically designed to be welded to another object.This business object is used by the NX and 4GD applications.

Cpd0WeldStud business object represents a weld in the NX application. This business object is authored and updated through NX. This object cannot be authored or updated through Teamcenter. It is a type of discrete join. It is attached to the Cpd0DesignElements with the Cpd0ConnectedElement relation. Cpd0WeldStud is the primary object in Cpd0ConnectedElement relation with Design Component. Stud weld is a fastener or specifically formed nut welded onto another metal part, typically called a base metal.This object is used by the NX and 4GD applications.

TcRuntimeType.description: Cpd0StructureExpandCursor represents a runtime business object for 4th Generation Design expand SOA operation support.This business object is also used internally in test classes to page content.This business object is intended primarily for internal usage and not meant to be used by other Teamcenter applications or customers.

TcRuntimeType.description: Cpd0SubsetLine is a runtime sub-type of BOMLine which wraps the subset in workset (Cpd0DesignSubsetElement in Cpd0WorksetRevision).The line_object of the Cpd0SubsetLine is the source Product Design (Cpd0CollaborativeDesign) as the subset is considered an occurrence of a subset of content from a source product design. The line's occurrence is the wrapped Cpd0DesignSubsetElement itself.Cpd0SubsetLine is used to present the subset in a user interface as it if was a child structure element under the workset as a parent ImanItemLine. Not all BOMLine interface methods are supported, as the occurrence of a subset in workset is not a normal BOM occurrence but rather specified as model content (Cpd0DesignSubsetElement is contained in a Cpd0WorksetModel which resides under a PSBomViewRevision of the owning Cpd0WorksetRevision.)Cpd0SubsetLine is used by 4GD applications and derivative applications. It is not expected to be extended or sub-typed.

TcProperty.description: A copy stable identity taken from the wrapped Cpd0DesignSubsetElement. This identity is unique within the owning Cpd0WorksetRevision. If the owning workset revision is copied or revised, this stable identity will remain unchanged and can be used to correlate copied subsets to original subsets.Since the value is derived from cpd0cs_id on Cpd0DesignSubsetElement which does permit a NULL value, an empty string may be returned from this property. However, the server attempts to always generate and save a value for the cpd0cs_id attribute on Cpd0DesignSubsetElement.
Runtime property that refers to UIDs of possibly relevant clearance calculations with the configuration criteria of the subset line.

TcRuntimeType.description: Cpd0WorksetLine is a subtype of ImanItemLine that adds the behavior of containing subsets (Cpd0DesignSubsetElement / CpdSubsetLine) of realized elements from source Product Designs (Cpd0CollaborativeDesign).A Workset line may be expanded inside a BOMWindow to access its contained subsets (see cpd0areSubsetsVisible property).Cpd0WorksetLine may be sub-classed to correlate with sub-types of Cpd0Workset/Cpd0WorksetRevision.

TcProperty.description: cpd0areSubsetsVisible is a runtime Boolean value to set/unset, that controls whether or not normal BOMLine expansion operations will return Cpd0SubsetLines as children (if there are any subsets in the workset wrapped by the workset line) in addition to any normal BOMLines. 4GD (4th Generation Design) expansion operations will understand to automatically set this value or use behaviors that ignore this control value.

TcStandardType.description: Cpd0ClearanceCalculation represents a subset of an Application Model (Mdl0ApplicationModel) based on a stored Recipe (ApprSearchCriteria) that is executed to view the subset content.The subset content is the model content objects that match the recipe's search criteria and unlike its parent (Fnd0RecipeContainer), all the search criteria is applied only to the referenced model (via mdl0model_object ).Cpd0ClearanceCalculation is used in 4GD-ClearanceDB integration. Cpd0ClearanceCalculation allows for different access control and simpler integration by separating out Clearance specific subsets from other ad-hoc subsets.

Cpd0DesignSubsetElement represents the realization of a subset of Cpd0CollaborativeDesign model content within a workset (Cpd0Workset).Cpd0DesignSubsetElement objects may be either created with explicit content or a search recipe or created by a realization of Mdl0SubsetDefinition (which stores a search recipe) into a Cpd0Workset, and these can contain one of more Cpd0DesignElement and Cpd0DesignFeature objects. The entire set of content of a Cpd0DesignSubsetElement can be positioned in the Cpd0Workset but not individual realized elements, as position overrides are not supported and the relative positions are maintained as found in the source application model.The Cpd0DesignSubsetElement remembers the content from the last replay of the stored recipe. The recipe is not executed automatically during load of the Cpd0DesignSubsetElement object, explicit user action is needed to replay it.Cpd0DesignSubsetElement objects are commonly used in 4th Generation Design and CAD applications such as NX.

The Cpd0DesignSubsetInstance business object manages realization of product design content into another model (e.g. a Cpd0WorksetModel managed by a Cpd0Workset object.). The outcome of this will be the realization of zero or more Cpd0DesignElement or Cpd0DesignFeature (such as welds or routings) objects. All realized content is only persistent in the source model and only logical present in the Cpd0WorksetModel.If a recipe is copied from one Cpd0DesignSubsetInstance object into another (from same Cpd0CollaborativeDesign), the effect is to append source recipe to the target recipe.The Cpd0DesignSubsetInstance is used by 4th Generation Design application, and it is a generic business object that can be extended if/as necessary.

Cpd0Workset is a concrete subclass of item that represents conjoined BOM content and 4GD (4th Generation Design) content such as design model elements (Cpd0DesignModelElement) and design features (Cpd0DesignFeature).The BOM content is held just as normal BOM Structure, but the 4GD model content is referenced by subsets (Cpd0DesignSubsetElement) in a workset model (Cpd0WorksetModel) that references a PSBomViewRevision structured under a Cpd0WorksetRevision.This combined structure is used by CAD tools as a collaboration work area that collects sets of data (using the subsets) from one or more source application models (Mdl0ApplicationModel).A Cpd0Workset (and corresponding Cpd0WorksetRevision) cannot be instantiated into any other context such as another item or application model, except for a NXBooklet Item (see preference TCAllowedParentTypes_Cpd0Workset that is set to NX0BookletItem )
Form Storage object for "Cpd0WorksetMaster" business object

Cpd0WorksetModel is a container for Workset (Cpd0Workset/Cpd0WorksetRevision) content.One model will exist for each BOMViewRevision of a WorksetRevision that has once been given a subset (Cpd0DesignSubsetElement) to contain.It has Model behavior and all contained subsets reference the Cpd0WorksetModel via their mdl0model_object property.It is used in 4GD (4th Generation Design) applications and derivative applications and should not need to be extended or sub-typed by any application.
Form Storage object for "Cpd0WorksetRevisionMaster" business object

ServiceInterface.description:
This service contains operations for creating and editing content within a Cpd0CollaborativeDesign. Operations are provided for the following:
    • Create and update of Cpd0DesignElements, Cpd0DesignFeatures, Cpd0DesignControlElements and Cpd0DesignSubsetElements within Cpd0Worksets.
    • Create and update of Cpd0SubsetItemRevision.
    • Substitution of Cpd0DesignElement source objects (and resulting transition of design component category)
    • Configured navigation of relationships.
    • Generate design context.

ServiceInterface.description:
This service exposes operations pertaining to update Realization of objects instantiated under workset revision.
It contains model configuration statements needed to specify how a source model (e.g. product design) should be configured prior to being realized. It also contains a recipe which describes what content from the source model should be selected for processing. The recipe can contain criteria for object attributes, spatial proximity, and for partition membership.
ServiceInterface.name: Realization

ServiceInterface.description: This service handles expansion of worksets, their subsets, and subordinate design components. This service is used mainly when opening a workset in a CAD tool or displaying the content of a workset in the Teamcenter client. The main operation supported by this service is startExpandStructure. There are two supporting operations nextExpandStructure and stopExpandStructure which complement startExpandStructure.

StructElement.description:
This contains property data for the newly created object. It is a map of property and values for the newly created object. All property values are expressed in their string equivalent. Struct.description:
ControlModelInfo is used as input to describe control model relations between a Cpd0DesignControlElement and the Cpd0DesignElements and the Cpd0DesignFeatures generated from the control model (e.g. mechanical routing or weld seam) managed by the design control element.

At a minimum, applications must specify the secondaryObject (the DesignElement or DesignFeature). Normally, applications will want to keep track, internally, how this relation maps to the applications data model. In that case, the application should set the clientId for new relations, the corresponding relation and csId will be returned to the application in a map based on the input clientId. (Note: the clientId values must unique within the entire input set).

If the application is intending to replace a connected part relation with another relation having the same copy stable ID then the applicaiton may pass the original csId as input and Teamcenter will use that to remove and replace the relation having that csId. If the csId is not specified Teamcenter will generate them automatically.

Struct.description:
DesignControlElementsInfo is used as input to describe create or update request for a Cpd0DesignControlElement. New Cpd0DesignControlElement objects require creation of a new Cpd0ShapeDesign objects.
Transform and bounding box can be optionally specified. Note: Changing the transform of a control model in Teamcenter does not affect a change in position of the elements that it produced.
Changes to Cpd0ControlModel relations are passed as a set of delta (adds,removed,replace, delete) requests.
    • The add requests from new relations.
    • The remove requests discard existing relations.
    • The replace requests do a remove and an add retaining the same csIS on the new relation that existed on the old;the copy stable ID(csId) must be specified in the ControlModelInfo for any requests.
    • The delete requests discard the existing relation and then attempts to delete the object it referenced.

Effectivity is specified in attrInfo in its string form via the mdl0effectivity_formula property. Effectivity is applied after control model relation updates. The effectivity condition can be cascaded to the design components and features that were generated/updated by the design control element. The cascade of effectivity takes into considerations the fact that the controlled elements may be shared between (revisions of) design control elements and, in that case, applies a combined effectivity of each revision to the shared elements.There may be cases when effectivity cannot be cascaded to a design component or feature (e.g. it may be owned by a different site). In that case, a warning is generated and the change will need to be reconciled manually.
Struct.name: DesignControlElementsInfo

Struct.description:
This filter can specify a combination of the type of the relation to traverse, the possible attributes on the relation, and the type of Business Object at the other end of that relation. An empty string denotes no filter (acts as a wildcard returning all objects without filtering the particular aspect that is not specified).

The combination of filters specified by relatedTypeName, all filters and otherSideObjectTypeName are combined together with a logical AND operation, meaning all criteria must be met for the related object to be returned to the caller.

WARNING: Any attribute filter other than mdl0cs_id, if passed in, will cause a not mplemented error and a service exception. This service may be extended in the future to support filtering on any relation attribute.

StructElement.description:
A set of name value pairs used to specify additional property data for design control elements. All values are specified as strings, the caller is responsible for generating the correct string representation of each value passed. For tag values, the UID of the tag is used. To carry Variant expressions and Occurrence Effectivity expressions from source objects to corresponding subordinate design components during realization, the properties rlz0sync_variant_exprs and rlz0sync_effectivity_exprs must be set to true accordingly. If closure rule is expected to be used as part of Item Realization, rlz0ClosureRule attribute should contain closure rule name. Closure rule will need to respect below validations.

Closure rule validation details:
1.    Closure rule name is valid (closure rule object with that name exists)
2.    Closure rule have associated closure rule clause(s)
3.    Closure rule is self-sufficient i.e. it does not require any parameterized information for evaluation.

attrInfo parameter : Map of (std::string, std::string[])

A set of name value pairs used to specify additional property data for design control elements. All values are specified as strings, the caller is responsible for generating the correct string representation of each value passed. For tag values, the UID of the tag is used. To carry Variant expressions and Occurrence Effectivity expressions from source objects to corresponding subordinate design components during realization, the properties rlz0sync_variant_exprs and rlz0sync_effectivity_exprs must be set to true accordingly. If closure rule is expected to be used as part of Item Realization, rlz0ClosureRule attribute should contain closure rule name. Closure rule will need to respect below validations.

Closure rule validation details:
1.    Closure rule name is valid (closure rule object with that name exists)
2.    Closure rule have associated closure rule clause(s)
3.    Closure rule is self-sufficient i.e. it does not require any parameterized information for evaluation.

OperationTemplate.description: Terminates an expansion initially started by a call to <font face="courier" height="10">startExpandStructure</font>. Clients should only call this operation when there are still results to return, as indicated by the <font face="courier" height="10">finished</font> flag being set to false in the last response from either startExpandStructure or <font face="courier" height="10">nextExpandStructure</font> operations.
OperationTemplate.name: Cpd0::Soa::CpdCore::StructureExpand::stopExpandStructure
OperationTemplate.returnDescription: Return value is always false.

OperationParameter.description: An expand cursor initially returned from <font face="courier" height="10">startExpandStructure</font>
OperationParameter.name: expandCursor

OperationTemplate.description:
Creates or updates a set of design control element (Cpd0DesignControlElement) objects and their relations to the design components and design features that they conntrol. Design control elements are used to represent welds seams (made up of multiple individual welds), and mechanical routings (such as piping system) which follow a path and are manifested by multiple design components and design features (welds) that make up the physical implementation of the routing. Design control elements are related to the design components and design features they control via a relation (Cpd0ControlModel).
Using this API, applications can create and update design control element (and relation) information in bulk, giving better through put that might not otherwise be achieved using standard object create and update API.

Cpd0ControlModel relationships have a copy stable ID which is unique within the scope of the design feature. The copy stable ID can be specified on create; if not specified, they will be automatically generated by Teamcenter. As their name suggests, when a design feature is copied the connected element relationships are also copied and the copy stable ID of the copied relations remains the same. The copy stable ID is used by external applications, like CAD, to correlate internal data to the related objects.
OperationTemplate.name: Cpd0::Soa::CpdCore::DataManagement::createOrUpdateDesignControlElements
OperationTemplate.returnDescription: The response contains a map of input caller specified client ID values and the corresponding objects that were created/updated features ( String/Business Object reference). The response also contains a map of caller specified client ID values for (connected element) relations and their corresponding copy stable ID values. The service data contains a list of added, updated, or deleted objects and it also contains a list of any errors which occurred within the call.

OperationParameter.description: The input set of information describing the design control elements to be created or updated.
OperationParameter.name: elementInfos

OperationTemplate.description:
Create or update Design Components(Cpd0DesignElement) of categories shape, promissory, reuse and subordinate in an application model (Cpd0CollaborativeDesign) based on input structure.
Creation of new shape design components includes creation of new ShapeDesign and ShapeDesignRevision objects. Creation of reuse design component forces creation of subordinate design components if the source item revision has structure. Position and effectivity information for new or updated design components can be set using this operation.
OperationTemplate.name: Cpd0::Soa::CpdCore::DataManagement::createOrUpdateDesignElements
OperationTemplate.returnDescription:
It contains a map of input client ID to the objects that were created or updated. It also returns a map of returned subordinates; where key is reuse design components and value is a vector of subordinate design components. Number of subordinates returned is governed by the levelsOfSubordinatesToReturn value specified on input for each reuse design components. It also returns ShapeDesign and ShapeDesignRevision pair of objects for those newly created.

The following partial errors may be returned:
    • 283518-Model Element and/or Copy Stable ID is not specified.
    • 283519-Design Feature object is not specified.
    • 283520-Connected Element is not specified.
    • 283521-The Connected objects do not exist in the same Collaborative Design as the Design Feature.
    • 283522-Business Object Type is not specified.

OperationParameter.description:
This Input contains a set of design components to be created or updated. The design components could be of category shape, reuse, subordinate or promissory based on arguments populated in the input structure (CreateOrUpdateDesignElementInfo). The same information is used to create or update initial values on design components and related objects

The inputs are separated based on category of design components. For example, inorder to create a promissory design component, it is expected to populate PromissoryDesignElementInfo, similarly with other categories of design components.

As explained in the above listed structures,
    • ShapeDesignElementInfo is to create or update shape design components.
    • PromissoryDesignElementInfo is to create or update promissory design components.
    • ReuseDesignElementInfo is to create or update reuse and subordinate design components.
OperationParameter.name: input

OperationTemplate.description:
Create or update Design Components(Cpd0DesignElement) of categories "shape", "promissory", "reuse" and "subordinate" in an application model (Cpd0CollaborativeDesign) based on input structure.
Creation of new "shape" design components includes creation of new ShapeDesign and ShapeDesignRevision objects. Creation of "reuse" design component forces creation of "subordinate" design components if the source item revision has structure. Position and effectivity information for new or updated design components can be set using this operation. For subordinate design component, if position information is present for updated design component, a position override will be created on the surbodinate design component. For reuse and subordinate design component, shape override will created/updated when geometryOverrideDatasetInput is present.Override added to reuse and subordinate design component can be removed by this operation.
OperationTemplate.name: Cpd0::Soa::CpdCore::DataManagement::createOrUpdateDesignElements
OperationTemplate.returnDescription: It contains a map of input client ID to the objects that were created or updated. It also returns a map of returned subordinates; where key is reuse design components and value is a vector of subordinate design components. Number of subordinates returned is governed by the levelsOfSubordinatesToReturn value specified on input for each reuse design components. It also returns ShapeDesign and ShapeDesignRevision pair of objects for those newly created.

OperationParameter.description:
This input contains a set of design components to be created or update. The design components could be of category "shape", "reuse", "subordinate" or "promissory" based on arguments populated in the input structure (CreateOrUpdateDesignElementsInfo). The same information is used to create or update initial values on design components and related objects.

The inputs are separated based on category of design components. For example, in order to create a "promissory" design component, it is expected to populate PromissoryDesignElementInfo, similarly with other categories of design components.
OperationParameter.name: input

OperationTemplate.description:
Creates or updates a list of design feature (Cpd0DesignFeature) objects and their relations to the design components they connect. Design features are used to represent welds (arc and spot), adhesive beads, etc. Design features are related to the design components they connect via a relation (Cpd0ConnectedElement).

Using this API, applications can create and update design feature information in bulk, giving better through put that might not otherwise be achieved using standard object create and update API.

Cpd0ConnectedElement relationships have a copy stable ID which is unique within the scope of the design feature. The copy stable ID can be specified on create; if not specified, they will be automatically generated by Teamcenter. As their name suggests, when a design feature is copied the connected element relationships are also copied and the copy stable ID of the copied relations remains the same. The copy stable ID is used by external applications, like CAD, to correlate internal data to the related items.
OperationTemplate.name: Cpd0::Soa::CpdCore::DataManagement::createOrUpdateDesignFeatures
OperationTemplate.returnDescription:
The response contains a map of input caller specified client ID values and the corresponding objects that were created/updated features. The response also contains a map of caller specified client ID values for (connected element) relations and their corresponding copy stable ID values. The service data contains a list of added, updated, or deleted objects and it also contains a list of any errors which occurred within the call.

The following partial errors may be returned:
    • 283518 -> Model Element and/or Copy Stable ID are not specified.
    • 283519 -> Design Feature object is not specified.
    • 283520 -> Connected Element is not specified.
    • 283521 -> The Connected objects do not exist in the same Collaborative Design as the Design Feature.
    • 283522 -> Business Object Type is not specified.

OperationParameter.description: The input list of design feature information describing the features to be created or updated.
OperationParameter.name: featureInfos

OperationTemplate.description:
This operation is used to create or update workset Subset and Design Subset Elements (Cpd0DesignSubsetElements) in a workset (Cpd0Workset). A Workset acts as a collector of design components (Cpd0DesignElements) instantiated from one or more Product Designs (Cpd0CollaborativeDesigns). It allows creating local copies of workset subsets to update. It can contain subsets or item assemblies as its direct children. The subset design component content is precise and Teamcenter does not automatically update it with changes to the source data.
            
The elements to be appended or removed to/from the Workset subset can be either an explicit list of elements or results from a Recipe.

When a designelement from a Product Design is realized into a subset in a
workset, the same design component is referenced in both the Product Design and
the workset. Changes made to this design component in a workset are visible in
the Product Design and vice versa.

Once workset subset is created using this operation, Realization Service operation like updateWorksetSubsetContent can be used to update workset subset content.
OperationTemplate.name: Cpd0::Soa::CpdCore::DataManagement::createOrUpdateDesignSubsetElements
OperationTemplate.returnDescription: A list of <font face="courier" height="10">DesignSubsetElementData</font> which is one to one correspondence with input <font face="courier" height="10">subsetInfos</font>.

OperationParameter.description: Data on <font face="courier" height="10">DesignSubsetElementInfo</font> used to create or update <font face="courier" height="10">DesignSubsetElements</font> in a workset.
OperationParameter.name: subsetInfos

OperationTemplate.description:
Query, filter, and configure all primary objects attached to the given input set of secondary objects. Filter criteria are provided through the RelatedObjectInput construct. Filtering can be based on the type of the relation, the type of the related object, and relation attribute values. Configuration conditions are specified by a ConfigurationContext object, which provides revision and unit effectivity rule information.
Returned objects are configured by the given configuration context and are access checked before being returned. An empty vector of RelatedObjectInput results in an invalid input exception being thrown.
RESTRICTION: Currently this API is only supported for navigation of Mdl0CopyStableRelation and its subtypes.
OperationTemplate.name: Cpd0::Soa::CpdCore::DataManagement::queryRelatedPrimaryObjects
OperationTemplate.returnDescription: A set of objects that are access checked before being returned. An empty list of <font face="courier" height="10">RelatedObjectInput</font> results in an invalid input exception being thrown.

OperationParameter.description: Configuration criteria to apply to the filtered set of related primary objects. Objects not satisfying the configuration criteria will not be returned.
OperationParameter.name: configurationContext

OperationParameter.description: A set of secondary objects and the filter criteria.
OperationParameter.name: inputObjects

OperationTemplate.description:

Filtering can be based on the type of the relation, the type of the related object, and relation property values. Configuration conditions are specified by a ConfigurationContext object, which provides revision and unit effectivity rule information.
Returned objects are configured by the given configuration context and are access checked before being returned. An empty vector of RelatedObjectInput results in an invalid input exception being thrown.
RESTRICTION: Currently this API is only supported for navigation of Mdl0CopyStableRelation and its subtypes.
OperationTemplate.name: Cpd0::Soa::CpdCore::DataManagement::queryRelatedSecondaryObjects
OperationTemplate.returnDescription:
A set of objects that are access checked before being returned. An empty list of RelatedObjectInput results in an invalid input exception being thrown.

NOTE: The input and response for this operation are identical to getRelatedPrimaryObject. The only difference between the operations is the direction of navigation across the relationship. Please see getRelatedPrimaryObject documentation for a detailed description of RelatedObjectInput and RelatedObjectsResponse.

OperationParameter.description: Configuration criteria to apply to the filtered set of related secondary objects. Objects not satisfying the configuration criteria will not be returned.
OperationParameter.name: configurationContext

OperationParameter.description: A set of primary objects and the filter criteria.
OperationParameter.name: inputObjects

1) The input structures relaxes the restriction on appendSourceElements, removeSourceElements, and subordinateSourceElements to be Mdl0ConditionalElement objects instead of Mdl0PositionedModelElement. Same restriction is removed from the returned output data.
2) The sourceModel can be specified to be a Baseline Revision in place of the usual Product Design. In this case the content of the Design Subset Element will scoped by the Baseline content.

A Workset acts as a collector of design components (Cpd0DesignElements) instantiated from one or more Product Designs (Cpd0CollaborativeDesigns). It allows creating local copies of workset subsets to update. It can contain subsets or item assemblies as its direct children. The subset design component content is precise and Teamcenter does not automatically update it with changes to the source data.
            
The elements to be appended or removed to/from the Workset subset can be either an explicit list of elements or results from a Recipe.

When a designelement from a Product Design is realized into a subset in a
workset, the same design component is referenced in both the Product Design and
the workset. Changes made to this design component in a workset are visible in
the Product Design and vice versa.

OperationTemplate.description:
The operation Instantiates model content (Design Model Elements) from one application model into another application model thereby creating a new "modelreuse" and "subordinate" states of subtypes of design model elements (Cpd0DesignModelElement) in the target model. Source model can be an Application Model (Mdl0ApplicationModel) or a Subset Definition (Mdl0SubsetDefinition). Each Target object (subordinate) in target model refers to a corresponding source object in the source model, allowing for an update of the target model.

The newly created objects in the target model are fully populated meaning they are persistently created in the context of the source model and will have a different life cycle than the related objects in the source model. The category of the realized model elements in the target model is always "subordinate". For example, a Design Component (Cpd0DesignElement) of category shape from a source model is realized into a target model, the category of the newly created object in the target model will be set to 'subordinate'.

OR Data on ModelToModelInstantiationInfo used to create or update Model to Model Instantiation across different Application Models.

OperationTemplate.description:
This operation returns a set of product configurations managed at the configurator level, e.g. for product tracking or reporting purposes.
Teamcenter variant configurators manage product configurations as VariantRules which are attached to an ItemRevision representing the product using any relationship type (see also preference TC_Default_SVR_Relationship). The product is identified by productName and productNameSpace parameters. Teamcenter configurators use the ID of the product item for productName, and the revision ID for productNameSpace. The identifiers of the product associated with a Product Design (Cpd0CollaborativeDesign) can be obtained from properties Mdl0ApplicationModel::get_mdl0var_conf_prod_name and Mdl0ApplicationModel::get_mdl0var_conf_prod_namespace.
getProductConfigurations returns both the old style and the new style variant rules attached to the item
OperationTemplate.name: Cpd0::Soa::CpdCore::DataManagement::getProductConfigurations
OperationTemplate.returnDescription:
This operation returns a list of Variant Criteria (Variant Rules) associated with the product. The following partial errors may be returned in service data:
92002: The Product Name and Product Namespace must not be empty.

OperationParameter.description: Identifies the product. It is used in conjunction with parameter productNameSpace to resolve potential ambiguity in variant option value names, and to identify product context specific constraints. Teamcenter configurators use a Multiple Field Key (MFK) stable identifier (see property Item::fnd0VariantNamespace) of the product item for productName. The productName value for a Product Design (Cpd0CollaborativeDesign) can be obtained from property Mdl0ApplicationModel::mdl0config_product_name.
OperationParameter.name: productName

OperationParameter.description: Specifies the namespace for the product identifier. It is used in conjunction with parameter productName to resolve potential ambiguity in variant option value names, and to identify product context specific constraints. Teamcenter configurators use the Revision ID of the product ItemRevision for productNameSpace. The productNameSpace value for a Product Design (Cpd0CollaborativeDesign) can be obtained from property Mdl0ApplicationModel::mdl0config_prod_namespace.
OperationParameter.name: productNameSpace
